disease_label_per_paper: Philadelphia chromosome-positive lymphoid blast crisis of chronic myeloid leukemia presenting with bilateral serous retinal detachment
presentation_summary: 36-year-old Asian man was admitted with severe general fatigue after fever and anemia had been treated at a local clinic two months earlier.
Physical examination showed hepatomegaly and splenomegaly. CBC showed hemoglobin 54 g/L, WBC 38.2 x10^9/L, platelets 214 x10^9/L, and 51.5% blast cells.
He had decreased vision for one month; ophthalmic examination showed bilateral serous retinal detachment involving the fovea, considered ocular involvement secondary to blast crisis.

outcome: Two months after starting induction therapy, fundus examination and OCT showed complete resolution of bilateral serous retinal detachment and improved vision.
